details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: lines ~340-429 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The selector does not enforce the documented 72-hour cutoff against each session’s `created_at`, so stale sessions on the boundary page can be selected for automatic resume.
  WHY: A stale session can consume a per-wake resume slot ahead of a recent stop, despite the documented manual fallback for sessions older than 72 hours.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: line 62 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The pickup hardcodes every resume trigger’s `run_once_at` to two minutes from now instead of using that resume entry’s `fire_offset_minutes`.
  WHY: All resumed sessions fire together, recreating the burst the spacing is intended to prevent.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: lines 68-94 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The pickup specifies pacing of 10 `create_trigger` calls per minute rather than the documented maximum of 8.
  WHY: The observed trigger-creation rate limit is about 9 calls per minute, so this pace can cause refused calls and delay resumes.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: lines 1-435 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The root selector copy is not byte-equal to its template twin and lacks the twin’s fire-offset, trigger fallback, and checker pagination/repository-matching changes.
  WHY: The parity test fails, and the pickup uses the stale root copy; this also leaves the root `_bound_wakes` without the `run_once_at` fallback, which can cause pending one-shot triggers to be treated as unreadable.
- changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md: lines 28-31 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The operator guidance says stalled projects resume within one pickup wake despite the documented 20-session per-wake cap.
  WHY: Backlogs larger than 20 sessions require later wakes to clear, so the statement gives operators an inaccurate recovery expectation.
- README.md: lines 1264-1270 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A paragraph break and indentation separate “An issue therefore waits...” from the queue paragraph it continues.
  WHY: The sentence’s antecedent becomes ambiguous and can be misread as introducing the usage-limit resume block.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:_decode_json_text (line not stated) | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The candidate-position slice applies to the string literal `"{["` rather than to the list comprehension result, so `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES` is not enforced.
  WHY: Inputs with many bracket characters can cause more than the documented maximum of 50 decode attempts.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The pickup must set each resume trigger’s `run_once_at` using that entry’s `fire_offset_minutes`, measured from trigger creation.
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, step 1a.3
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md line 62 retains “two minutes from now” instead of reading `fire_offset_minutes`; tests assert the per-entry offset text.
- requirement: The pickup must pace `create_trigger` at most 8 calls per minute across the wake.
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, steps 1a.4 and 3
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md lines 68-71 and 94 retain “about 10 calls per minute,” “After every 10th,” and “same 10 per minute”; tests assert 8-per-minute pacing.
- requirement: `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` must remain byte-equal to its `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` twin.
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` is 435 lines and lacks changes present in the 464-line template twin; `tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py::test_template_parity` asserts equality.
- requirement: The changelog recovery statement must account for the 20-session per-wake cap and say recovery continues in capped batches rather than implying all stalled projects resume within one wake.
  expected_change_site: changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md, “What this means for operators” paragraph
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md documents a 20-session per-wake cap and 47 stopped sessions, while its recovery statement promises completion within one pickup wake.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py | select() function, the per-session loop (lines ~368-402); no created_at inspection anywhere in the module | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The selector does not enforce the documented 72-hour session-age cutoff using `created_at`.
  WHY: A session 8 days old with a stale usage-limit status_detail can be selected ahead of a recent stop and consume one of the 20 per-wake resume slots.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md | step 1a.3, line 62 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The pickup schedules every resume trigger two minutes from now instead of using its `fire_offset_minutes`.
  WHY: All resumed sessions fire together, recreating the burst that the fire spacing was designed to prevent.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md | step 1a.4, line 68 ("about 10 calls per minute" / "After every 10th") and line 94 ("same 10 per minute") | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The pickup paces trigger creation at 10 calls per minute instead of the documented maximum of 8.
  WHY: A batch of resume triggers plus queue-session triggers can exceed the observed rate limit and delay remaining resumes.
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py (root copy, lines 1-435) vs workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py (twin, lines 1-464) | the entire file | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root copy is not byte-equal to its template twin and lacks the twin’s offset, trigger fallback, and checker changes.
  WHY: The parity test fails, and the pickup’s root script lacks the twin’s pending-resume handling and repository-verified checker guard.
- changelog.d/5660-resume-usage-limit-stops.md | line 28, "after a usage-limit stop, stalled projects resume within one pickup wake of the reset" | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The changelog says stalled projects resume within one pickup wake despite the 20-session per-wake cap and the documented 47-session incident.
  WHY: At least three hourly wakes are needed to clear that backlog.
